reasons: Depends on a hard-coded count of 41 findings.
Reviews are only valid for the reviewed values; a later change blocks the commit.

terms.meaning: keep the review and sources on record but leave the number blank so it is not shown
a project with all the required budget and schedule fields filled in

sections.name: File setup, digest, live, ready, ids
sections.title: Setup and readiness rules
sections.what: Loads libraries, reads the findings file, checks it has 41 entries, and defines how a project counts as scan-ready.
sections.why: The count check stops the script if the findings file changed unexpectedly.
sections.watch_out: A project is scan-ready only when every required field has a value, so holding a value changes this.

sections.name: units
sections.title: Units for each field
sections.what: Returns the unit for a field: months for delays, raw currency for dairy, and millions otherwise.
sections.why: The unit is recorded with each held value so the review is understood later.
sections.watch_out: Dairy is the only industry with raw currency units here.

sections.name: main (part 1)
sections.title: Verify mode and the plan
sections.what: In verify mode, checks the committed review through the detail page. Otherwise, builds the plan for each reviewed project and skips projects that already carry the same review.
sections.why: Likely reason: re-running must not overwrite a review that was already applied.
sections.watch_out: A changed existing review stops the script for manual review.

sections.name: main: if
sections.title: Commit and output
sections.what: When committed, checks the fingerprint, writes each review and the blanks, logs the changes, confirms nothing else changed, and prints the result.
sections.why: The checks keep the commit limited to the held fields.
sections.watch_out: Output file names are chosen so an earlier committed file is not overwritten.

summary: Holds back numbers from 41 reviewed findings where the sources do not support them, by blanking the value and recording the review, while leaving all other project data untouched.
purpose: Makes sure unsupported budget and delay figures are not shown as facts, and keeps the reason and sources visible.
why: The script's checks say the held values must not be restored by mistake, which suggests the review is deliberate.
how: Reads the findings file and checks it has 41 entries. Builds a plan for each project, showing what would be held. Without --commit it only prints the plan. With --commit it checks the approved fingerprint, writes the review and blank values, logs each change, and confirms nothing else moved.
inputs: The continued-research findings JSON in the evidence-repair data folder, the database, and the --commit and --approve flags.
outputs: A dry-run or committed JSON file under the data folder and change log rows when committed.
risks: Blanks real budget and delay values. Wrong findings would hide correct numbers from the scan.
debug: Read the dry-run output's rows list. For a project that was not expected to change, compare its stored value and review record.
